ko.R: 세상의 왕들은 세금과 통행료를 거둔다. 그들은 누구에게서 그것을 거두느냐?

pt.L: Os reis da terra, de quem cobram tributos ou imposto?
pt.B: Quando os reis da terra cobram tributos ou impostos, quem paga?
pt.R: Os reis deste mundo cobram impostos e taxas. De quem eles cobram?

am.L: የምድር ነገሥታት ቀረጥን ወይም ግብርን ከማን ይቀበላሉ?
am.B: የምድር ነገሥታት ቀረጥ ወይም ግብር ሲቀበሉ የሚከፍላቸው ማን ነው?
am.R: የዚህ ዓለም ነገሥታት ቀረጥና ግብር ይሰበስባሉ። የሚሰበስቡት ከማን ነው?

ru.L: Цари земли с кого берут пошлины или подать?
ru.B: Когда земные цари берут пошлины или налоги, кто их платит?
ru.R: Цари этого мира собирают налоги и пошлины. С кого они их собирают?

hi.L: पृथ्वी के राजा, किनसे वे चुंगी या कर लेते हैं?
hi.B: जब पृथ्वी के राजा चुंगी या कर लेते हैं, तो उसे कौन चुकाता है?
hi.R: इस दुनिया के राजा कर और शुल्क वसूलते हैं। वे उन्हें किनसे वसूलते हैं?

uk.L: Царі землі з кого беруть мито чи податок?
uk.B: Коли земні царі беруть мито чи податки, хто їх платить?
uk.R: Царі цього світу збирають податки й мита. З кого вони їх збирають?

ja.L: 地上の王たちは、だれから関税や人頭税を取るのか？
ja.B: 地上の王たちが関税や税を取り立てるとき、それを納めるのはだれか？
ja.R: この世の王たちは、いろいろな税金を集める。だれから集めるのだろうか？

decisions.choice: tolls or tax: duties on goods and a tax on each person
decisions.reason: The first word means duties such as tolls on goods. The second, borrowed from Latin, is the tax paid by each person, the tax of 22:17-19.

decisions.choice: the kings of the earth: human rulers
decisions.reason: The phrase means rulers of this world, set against God as king (Psalm 2:2). The comparison leads to God and his house.

decisions.choice: a statement, then the question
decisions.reason: Readable states the fact and then asks the question.

decisions.choice: ushuru au kodi ya kichwa
decisions.reason: The two Greek words are duties on goods and a tax on each person (meaning decision m1). "Kodi ya kichwa" (head tax) shows the second at Literal; Balanced and Readable use the general words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "thuế quan hay thuế thân" (L); "thuế hàng hóa hay thuế thân" (B)
decisions.reason: Duties on goods and a tax on each person (meaning decision); "thuế thân" is the Vietnamese word for a poll tax.

decisions.choice: "땅의 왕들" (L), "세상 왕들" (B, R); "관세", "세금"
decisions.reason: The kings of the earth are human rulers (meaning decision); the two words are duties on goods and a tax on each person.

decisions.choice: "ቀረጥ" (duty, toll) and "ግብር" (tax)
decisions.reason: Amharic has the same pair the Greek has: "ቀረጥ" for duties charged on goods and "ግብር" for the tax a ruler lays on his people.

decisions.choice: "関税や人頭税" (L); "関税や税" (B); "いろいろな税金" (R)
decisions.reason: The two words are duties on goods and a tax on each person (m1); Literal names both, and Readable gathers them into one plain word.

source.text: ἀπὸ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῶν ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων;

records.literal_gloss: From the sons of them or from the strangers?

en.L: From their sons, or from strangers?"
en.B: From their own sons, or from people outside their family?"
en.R: Do they collect from their own sons, or from other people?"

es.L: ¿De sus hijos o de los extraños?».
es.B: ¿De sus propios hijos o de los que no son de su familia?».
es.R: ¿Se los cobran a sus propios hijos o a otras personas?».

fr.L: De leurs fils, ou des étrangers ? »
fr.B: Leurs propres fils, ou des gens étrangers à leur famille ? »
fr.R: Est-ce qu’ils les font payer à leurs propres fils, ou à d’autres gens ? »

sw.L: Kutoka kwa wana wao au kutoka kwa wageni?"
sw.B: Kwa wana wao wenyewe, au kwa watu wasio wa familia yao?"
sw.R: Je, huzikusanya kutoka kwa wana wao wenyewe, au kutoka kwa watu wengine?"

vi.L: Từ con cái của họ hay từ người ngoài?"
vi.B: Từ chính con cái của họ, hay từ những người ngoài gia đình?"
vi.R: Họ thu từ chính con cái mình, hay từ người khác?"

ko.B: 자기 아들들에게서냐, 아니면 집안사람이 아닌 남들에게서냐?"
ko.R: 자기 아들들에게서 거두느냐, 아니면 다른 사람들에게서 거두느냐?"

pt.L: Dos filhos deles ou dos estranhos?"
pt.B: Dos próprios filhos ou de gente de fora da família?"
pt.R: Eles cobram dos próprios filhos ou das outras pessoas?"

am.B: ከገዛ ልጆቻቸው ነው ወይስ ከቤተሰባቸው ውጭ ካሉ ሰዎች?
am.R: ከገዛ ልጆቻቸው ነው የሚሰበስቡት ወይስ ከሌሎች ሰዎች?

ru.L: С сыновей своих или с чужих?»
ru.B: Со своих собственных сыновей или с людей не из их семьи?»
ru.R: Со своих сыновей или с других людей?»

hi.L: अपने पुत्रों से, या परायों से?"
hi.B: अपने ही बेटों से, या परिवार के बाहर के लोगों से?"
hi.R: क्या वे अपने बेटों से वसूलते हैं, या दूसरे लोगों से?"

uk.L: Зі своїх синів чи з чужих?»
uk.B: Зі своїх синів чи з людей, що не належать до їхньої родини?»
uk.R: Зі своїх власних синів чи з інших людей?»

ja.L: 自分の子たちからか、それともよその者たちからか？」
ja.B: 自分の子たちからか、それとも家族以外の人たちからか？」
ja.R: 自分の子どもたちからか、それともほかの人たちからか？」

decisions.choice: strangers: people not of the king's family
decisions.reason: The word means those who belong to others. Here it is everyone outside the royal household, the king's subjects.

decisions.choice: sons, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The picture is of a king's household, and it leads to Jesus, God's Son (17:5, 26). The word is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: people outside their family
decisions.reason: Balanced says who the strangers are in this picture.

decisions.choice: "con cái" for "sons", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English keeps "sons" with no setting; Vietnamese "con cái" means the king's children, the family set against outsiders, which is the point (meaning decision), and "con trai" would narrow it needlessly. The picture still points to the Son in 17:26.

decisions.choice: "아들들" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The king's sons stand in the picture for the Son (meaning decision on 17:26), so, as in the English, there is no gender span here.

decisions.choice: "子たち" (L, B); "子どもたち" (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The king's sons lead to Jesus, God's Son (m1 of 17:26), so the word "子" is kept, which echoes "神の子" and "わたしの子" (17:5); "子" is not limited to males in Japanese, and no setting is needed.

source.text: εἰπόντος δέ· Ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων, ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἄρα γε ἐλεύθεροί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοί.

records.literal_gloss: Having said and, From the strangers, said to him the Jesus, Then indeed free are the sons.

en.L: And when he said, "From strangers," Jesus said to him, "Then the sons are free.
en.B: "From outsiders," Peter replied. Jesus said to him, "So the sons owe nothing.
en.R: Peter answered, "From other people." Jesus said to him, "Then the sons do not have to pay.

es.L: Y cuando él dijo: «De los extraños», Jesús le dijo: «Por tanto, los hijos están libres.
es.B: «De los de fuera», respondió Pedro. Jesús le dijo: «Entonces los hijos no deben nada.
es.R: Pedro respondió: «De otras personas». Jesús le dijo: «Entonces los hijos no tienen que pagar.

fr.L: Et comme il disait : « Des étrangers », Jésus lui déclara : « Les fils sont donc libres.
fr.B: « Les étrangers », répondit Pierre. Jésus lui dit : « Les fils ne doivent donc rien.
fr.R: Pierre a répondu : « Les autres gens. » Jésus lui a dit : « Alors les fils n’ont pas à payer.

sw.L: Naye aliposema, "Kutoka kwa wageni," Yesu akamwambia, "Basi wana wako huru.
sw.B: Petro alijibu, "Kutoka kwa watu wa nje." Yesu akamwambia, "Basi wana hawadaiwi kitu.
sw.R: Petro alijibu, "Kutoka kwa watu wengine." Yesu akamwambia, "Basi wana hawalazimiki kulipa.

vi.L: Và khi ông nói: "Từ người ngoài," Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Vậy thì con cái được miễn.
vi.B: Phi-e-rơ thưa: "Từ người ngoài." Đức Giê-xu bảo ông: "Vậy thì con cái không phải nộp gì cả.
vi.R: Phi-e-rơ trả lời: "Từ người khác." Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Vậy thì con cái không phải nộp thuế.

ko.L: 그가 "남들에게서입니다" 하고 말하자, 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "그렇다면 아들들은 자유롭다.
ko.B: 베드로가 "남들에게서 받습니다" 하고 대답하자, 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "그렇다면 아들들은 낼 의무가 없다.
ko.R: 베드로가 대답했다. "다른 사람들에게서 거둡니다." 그러자 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "그렇다면 아들들은 낼 필요가 없다.

pt.L: E, quando ele disse: "Dos estranhos", Jesus lhe disse: "Então os filhos são livres.
pt.B: "Dos de fora", respondeu Pedro. Jesus lhe disse: "Então os filhos não devem nada.
pt.R: Pedro respondeu: "Das outras pessoas." Jesus disse a ele: "Então os filhos não precisam pagar.

am.L: እርሱም፦ «ከባዕዳን» ባለ ጊዜ ኢየሱስ እንዲህ አለው፦ «እንግዲያስ ልጆቹ ነፃ ናቸው።
am.B: ጴጥሮስም፦ «ከውጭ ሰዎች» ብሎ መለሰ። ኢየሱስም እንዲህ አለው፦ «እንግዲያውስ ልጆቹ ምንም ዕዳ የለባቸውም።
am.R: ጴጥሮስም፦ «ከሌሎች ሰዎች» ብሎ መለሰ። ኢየሱስም እንዲህ አለው፦ «እንግዲያውስ ልጆቹ መክፈል የለባቸውም።

ru.L: Когда же он сказал: «С чужих», Иисус сказал ему: «Значит, сыновья свободны.
ru.B: «С посторонних», — ответил Пётр. Иисус сказал ему: «Значит, сыновья ничего не должны.
ru.R: Пётр ответил: «С других людей.» Иисус сказал ему: «Значит, сыновьям платить не нужно.

hi.L: जब उसने कहा, "परायों से," तो यीशु ने उससे कहा, "तब तो पुत्र स्वतंत्र हैं।
hi.B: "बाहरवालों से," पतरस ने उत्तर दिया। यीशु ने उससे कहा, "तो बेटों को कुछ नहीं देना होता।
hi.R: पतरस ने जवाब दिया, "दूसरे लोगों से।" यीशु ने उससे कहा, "तो बेटों को कर नहीं देना पड़ता।

uk.L: Коли ж він сказав: «З чужих», Ісус сказав йому: «Отже, сини вільні.
uk.B: «З чужих», — відповів Петро. Ісус сказав йому: «Тож сини нічого не винні.
uk.R: Петро відповів: «З інших людей.» Ісус сказав йому: «Тоді сини не мусять платити.

ja.L: 彼が「よその者たちからです」と言うと、イエスは彼に言われた。「それでは、子たちは自由である。
ja.B: 「家族以外の人たちからです」とペトロが答えると、イエスは言われた。「それなら、子たちは納めなくてよいのだ。
ja.R: ペトロは答えました。「ほかの人たちからです。」イエスはペトロに言われました。「それなら、子どもたちは納めなくてもいいのだ。

decisions.choice: the sons are free: God's Son owes no tax for his Father's house
alternatives: a statement about earthly kings only
a ruling that no Jew need pay the temple tax
decisions.reason: The temple tax was paid to God, the great king. Jesus is God's Son (17:5), so he owes nothing. The plural "sons" may include his disciples as God's children, since the coin pays for Peter too (17:27).

decisions.choice: then indeed: the conclusion follows from Peter's answer
decisions.reason: The words draw the conclusion Peter's own answer requires.

decisions.choice: owe nothing (B); do not have to pay (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "free" means in a talk about taxes.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

decisions.choice: "자유롭다" (L); "낼 의무가 없다" (B); "낼 필요가 없다" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word "free", which carries the meaning decision's point that God's Son owes no tax for his Father's house; Balanced and Readable say what the freedom is here.

source.text: ἵνα δὲ μὴ σκανδαλίσωμεν αὐτούς, πορευθεὶς εἰς θάλασσαν βάλε ἄγκιστρον καὶ τὸν ἀναβάντα πρῶτον ἰχθὺν ἆρον, καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εὑρήσεις στατῆρα· ἐκεῖνον λαβὼν δὸς αὐτοῖς ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ καὶ σοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: So that but not we may offend them, having gone to sea cast a hook and the having come up first fish take, and having opened the mouth of it you will find a stater; that having taken give to them for me and you.

en.L: But so that we do not offend them, go to [the] sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up, and when you open its mouth you will find a stater. Take that and give [it] to them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you."
en.B: Still, we do not want to give them a reason to take offense. So go down to the lake and throw in a hook. Take the first fish that comes up, open its mouth, and you will find {{units:a silver coin worth four days' wages|a stater}}. Take it and give it to them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and for you."
en.R: But we do not want to upset these men. So go to the lake and throw in a fishing line with a hook. Pull in the first fish you catch. Open its mouth, and you will find {{units:a silver coin worth four days' pay|a stater}}. That is enough to pay the tax for two people. Take it and give it to them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and for you."

es.L: Pero, para que no los escandalicemos, ve al mar, lanza un anzuelo y saca el primer pez que suba; y abriéndole la boca encontrarás un estatero. Toma esa [moneda] y dásela a ellos por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y por ti».
es.B: Sin embargo, no queremos darles motivo de ofensa. Así que ve al lago y echa un anzuelo. Saca el primer pez que pique, ábrele la boca y encontrarás {{units:una moneda de plata que vale cuatro días de salario|un estatero}}. Toma esa moneda y dásela a ellos por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y por ti».
es.R: Pero no queremos molestar a estos hombres. Así que ve al lago y echa un sedal con anzuelo. Saca el primer pez que pesques. Ábrele la boca y encontrarás {{units:una moneda de plata que vale lo que se gana en cuatro días|un estatero}}. Eso alcanza para pagar el impuesto de dos personas. Toma esa moneda y dásela a ellos por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y por ti».

fr.L: Mais pour que nous ne les scandalisions pas, va à la mer, jette un hameçon, et prends le premier poisson qui montera ; et, en lui ouvrant la bouche, tu trouveras un statère. Prends-le et donne-le-leur pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et pour toi. »
fr.B: Pourtant, nous ne voulons pas leur donner une raison d’être choqués. Va donc au lac et jette un hameçon. Prends le premier poisson qui mordra, ouvre-lui la bouche, et tu y trouveras {{units:une pièce d’argent valant quatre journées de salaire|un statère}}. Remets-leur cette somme pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et pour toi. »
fr.R: Mais nous ne voulons pas fâcher ces hommes. Alors va au lac et lance une ligne avec un hameçon. Tire hors de l’eau le premier poisson que tu attraperas. Ouvre-lui la bouche : tu y trouveras {{units:une pièce d’argent qui vaut quatre jours de salaire|un statère}}. Cela suffit pour payer la taxe de deux personnes. Va leur donner cet argent pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et pour toi. »

sw.L: Lakini ili tusiwakwaze, nenda baharini, utupe ndoano, umvue samaki wa kwanza atakayepanda, na ukimfungua mdomo utakuta stateri; ichukue hiyo, uwape badala {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na yako."
sw.B: Hata hivyo, hatutaki kuwapa sababu ya kuchukizwa. Kwa hiyo nenda ziwani, utupe ndoano. Mvue samaki wa kwanza atakayenaswa, umfungue mdomo, nawe utakuta {{units:sarafu ya fedha yenye thamani ya mshahara wa siku nne|stateri}}. Ichukue, uwape kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kwa ajili yako."
sw.R: Lakini hatutaki kuwaudhi watu hawa. Kwa hiyo nenda ziwani, utupe mshipi wenye ndoano. Mvute samaki wa kwanza utakayemvua. Fungua mdomo wake, nawe utakuta {{units:sarafu ya fedha yenye thamani ya mshahara wa siku nne|stateri}}. Inatosha kulipa kodi ya watu wawili. Ichukue, uwape kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kwa ajili yako."

vi.L: Nhưng để chúng ta khỏi làm cho họ vấp phạm, hãy ra biển, thả lưỡi câu, và bắt con cá nào cắn câu trước, mở miệng nó ra, con sẽ thấy một đồng sta-te. Hãy lấy đồng ấy và đưa cho họ thay cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và con."
vi.B: Tuy vậy, chúng ta không muốn làm cho họ vấp phạm. Vậy con hãy ra hồ thả câu. Con cá nào cắn câu trước, con hãy bắt lấy, mở miệng nó ra, con sẽ thấy {{units:một đồng bạc trị giá bốn ngày công|một đồng sta-te}}. Hãy lấy đồng ấy và đưa cho họ để nộp thuế cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và cho con."
vi.R: Nhưng chúng ta không muốn làm cho những người này bực mình. Vậy con hãy ra hồ thả cần câu có lưỡi câu xuống nước. Hãy kéo con cá đầu tiên con câu được lên. Mở miệng nó ra, con sẽ thấy {{units:một đồng bạc trị giá bốn ngày công|một đồng sta-te}}. Số tiền ấy đủ để nộp thuế cho hai người. Hãy lấy đồng ấy và đưa cho họ để nộp thuế cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và cho con."

ko.L: 그러나 우리가 그들을 걸려 넘어지게 하지 않도록, 바다로 가서 낚시를 던져라. 그리고 처음 올라오는 물고기를 잡아라. 그 입을 열면 스타테르 한 닢을 찾을 것이다. 그것을 가져다가 나와 너를 대신하여 그들에게 주어라."
ko.B: 그러나 우리가 그들의 비위를 거스를 까닭은 없다. 그러니 바다로 가서 낚시를 던져라. 처음 올라오는 물고기를 잡아 그 입을 열어 보면, {{units:나흘 품삯이 되는 은돈 한 닢|스타테르 한 닢}}을 찾을 것이다. 그것을 가져다가 나와 너의 몫으로 그들에게 주어라."
ko.R: 하지만 우리는 저 사람들의 마음을 상하게 하고 싶지 않다. 그러니 호수에 가서 낚싯줄을 던져라. 처음 잡히는 물고기를 끌어올려라. 그 입을 열어 보면 {{units:나흘 품삯이 되는 은돈 한 닢|스타테르 한 닢}}이 있을 것이다. 그것이면 두 사람의 세금을 낼 수 있다. 그것을 가져다가 나와 너의 세금으로 그들에게 주어라."

pt.L: Mas, para que não os escandalizemos, vá ao mar, jogue um anzol e pegue o primeiro peixe que subir; e, abrindo a boca dele, você encontrará um estáter. Pegue-o e dê a eles por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e por você."
pt.B: Mesmo assim, não queremos que eles tenham motivo para se ofender. Por isso, vá até o lago e jogue um anzol. Pegue o primeiro peixe que fisgar, abra a boca dele, e você vai encontrar {{units:uma moeda de prata que vale quatro dias de salário|um estáter}}. Pegue a moeda e entregue a eles por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e por você."
pt.R: Mas nós não queremos aborrecer esses homens. Então vá até o lago e jogue uma linha com anzol. Puxe o primeiro peixe que você pegar. Abra a boca dele, e você vai encontrar {{units:uma moeda de prata que vale quatro dias de pagamento|um estáter}}. Ela dá para pagar o imposto de duas pessoas. Pegue a moeda e entregue a eles por {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e por você."

am.L: ነገር ግን እንዳናሰናክላቸው ወደ ባሕር ሄደህ መንጠቆ ጣል፤ መጀመሪያ የሚወጣውንም ዓሣ ያዝ፤ አፉንም ስትከፍት እስታቴር ታገኛለህ፤ እርሱን ወስደህ ስለ እኔና ስለ አንተ ስጣቸው።»
am.B: ቢሆንም ቅር የሚሰኙበት ምክንያት ልንሰጣቸው አንፈልግም። ስለዚህ ወደ ሐይቁ ሄደህ መንጠቆ ጣል። መጀመሪያ የሚወጣውን ዓሣ ያዝ፤ አፉን ክፈት፤ {{units:የአራት ቀን ደመወዝ የሚያህል የብር ሳንቲም|አንድ እስታቴር}} ታገኛለህ። እርሱን ወስደህ ስለ እኔና ስለ አንተ ስጣቸው።»
am.R: ነገር ግን እነዚህን ሰዎች ማስቀየም አንፈልግም። ስለዚህ ወደ ሐይቁ ሂድና መንጠቆ ያለበት የዓሣ ማጥመጃ ገመድ ጣል። መጀመሪያ የምትይዘውን ዓሣ ጎትተህ አውጣ። አፉን ክፈት፤ {{units:የአራት ቀን ክፍያ የሚያህል የብር ሳንቲም|አንድ እስታቴር}} ታገኛለህ። ይህ ለሁለት ሰው ግብር ይበቃል። እርሱን ወስደህ ስለ እኔና ስለ አንተ ስጣቸው።»

ru.L: Но чтобы нам не заставить их споткнуться, пойди к морю, закинь крючок и возьми первую рыбу, которая попадётся, и, открыв ей рот, найдёшь статир; возьми его и отдай им за {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} и за себя.»
ru.B: И всё же мы не хотим давать им повода для обиды. Поэтому пойди к озеру и закинь крючок. Возьми первую рыбу, которая попадётся, открой ей рот, и ты найдёшь {{units:серебряную монету, равную заработку за четыре дня|статир}}. Возьми её и отдай им за {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} и за себя.»
ru.R: Но мы не хотим обижать этих людей. Поэтому пойди к озеру и закинь удочку с крючком. Вытащи первую рыбу, которую поймаешь. Открой ей рот, и ты найдёшь {{units:серебряную монету — плату за четыре дня работы|статир}}. Этого хватит, чтобы заплатить налог за двоих. Возьми её и отдай им за {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} и за себя.»

hi.L: परंतु इसलिए कि हम उन्हें ठोकर न खिलाएँ, तुम समुद्र पर जाकर काँटा फेंको, और पहली ऊपर आनेवाली मछली को उठा लो; उसका मुँह खोलोगे तो तुम्हें एक स्तातेर मिलेगा। उसे लेकर मेरी और अपनी ओर से उन्हें दे दो।"
hi.B: फिर भी हम उन्हें बुरा मानने का कोई कारण नहीं देना चाहते। इसलिए झील पर जाकर काँटा डालो। जो मछली पहले आए, उसे पकड़ लो, उसका मुँह खोलो, और तुम्हें {{units:चार दिन की मज़दूरी के बराबर चाँदी का एक सिक्का|एक स्तातेर}} मिलेगा। उसे लेकर मेरे लिए और अपने लिए उन्हें दे दो।"
hi.R: पर हम इन लोगों को नाराज़ नहीं करना चाहते। इसलिए झील पर जाओ और काँटेवाली डोरी पानी में डालो। जो पहली मछली पकड़ में आए, उसे बाहर निकालो। उसका मुँह खोलना, तो तुम्हें {{units:चार दिन की मज़दूरी के बराबर चाँदी का एक सिक्का|एक स्तातेर}} मिलेगा। वह दो लोगों का कर चुकाने के लिए काफ़ी है। उसे लेकर मेरे लिए और अपने लिए उन्हें दे दो।"

uk.L: А щоб ми не стали для них причиною спотикання, піди до моря, закинь гачок і візьми першу рибу, що вийде; і, відкривши їй рота, знайдеш статир. Узявши його, дай їм за {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} і [за] тебе.»
uk.B: Але ми не хочемо давати їм приводу обурюватися. Тож піди до озера й закинь гачок. Візьми першу рибу, що клюне, відкрий їй рота, і знайдеш там {{units:срібну монету вартістю чотириденного заробітку|статир}}. Цим заплати їм за {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} і за тебе.»
uk.R: Але ми не хочемо засмучувати цих людей. Тож піди до озера й закинь вудку з гачком. Витягни першу рибу, яку спіймаєш. Відкрий їй рота, і знайдеш там {{units:срібну монету, що коштує чотири денні заробітки|статир}}. Цього вистачить, щоб заплатити податок за двох. Цим і заплати їм за {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} і за тебе.»

ja.L: しかし、わたしたちが彼らをつまずかせないために、海に行って釣り針を投げ、最初に上って来た魚を取りなさい。そして、その口を開けると、スタテル[銀貨]一枚が見つかる。それを取って、わたしとあなたの分として彼らに納めなさい。」
ja.B: しかし、あの人たちをつまずかせないようにしよう。湖に行って釣り針を投げ、最初に釣れた魚を取りなさい。その口を開けると、{{units:四日分の賃金にあたる銀貨一枚|スタテル銀貨一枚}}が見つかる。それを取って、わたしとあなたの分として納めなさい。」
ja.R: でも、あの税金を集める人たちの気持ちを悪くさせないようにしよう。湖に行って、釣り針のついた糸を投げ入れなさい。最初に釣れた魚を引き上げなさい。その口を開けると、{{units:四日分の賃金にあたる銀貨一枚|スタテル銀貨一枚}}が見つかる。それで、二人分の税金を納めることができる。それを取って、わたしとあなたの分として、あの人たちに納めなさい。」

decisions.choice: offend them: give them cause to take offense
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause to stumble. Here it means giving the collectors and others a reason to think Jesus despised God's house.

decisions.choice: a stater: a silver coin worth four drachmas
decisions.reason: Four drachmas was about four days' wages, the tax for two men (17:24). One coin pays for Jesus and Peter together.

decisions.choice: for me and you: in payment for both
alternatives: in place of me but not of you
decisions.reason: The word means "in place of" or "in exchange for". The coin covers what each of them owed.

decisions.choice: the sea: the Sea of Galilee, beside Capernaum
decisions.reason: Capernaum lay on the shore of the lake. Matthew does not tell of Peter catching the fish; the story ends with Jesus's word.

decisions.choice: a silver coin worth four days' wages (B); a silver coin worth four days' pay (R); a stater (alternative)
decisions.reason: The Measures setting gives the original coin. Literal keeps "stater".

decisions.choice: the lake
decisions.reason: The Sea of Galilee is a lake, and Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: That is enough to pay the tax for two people.
decisions.reason: Readable says why one coin is enough for both.

decisions.choice: these men
decisions.reason: Readable says who might be upset: the men who collect the tax.

decisions.choice: el mar (L); el lago (B, R)
decisions.reason: The "sea" is the Sea of Galilee, beside Capernaum (meaning decision m4), a freshwater lake. Literal keeps the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say "lago", as the English does.

decisions.choice: {{units:una moneda de plata que vale cuatro días de salario|un estatero}}
decisions.reason: As in the English and in John 6:7, the coin is given in wages by default, with the Greek coin as the alternative (meaning decision m2). The following words say "esa moneda", which reads correctly with either form.

decisions.choice: scandaliser (L); leur donner une raison d’être choqués (B); fâcher (R)
decisions.reason: Here the verb means giving the collectors cause to take offense (m1), which is what modern French "scandaliser" says. In 18:6-9, where the same verb means causing someone to fall into sin, Literal says "faire trébucher".

decisions.choice: cette somme (B), cet argent (R) for "it"
decisions.reason: Under the Measures setting the coin is either "une pièce" (feminine) or "un statère" (masculine), so a pronoun would agree with only one of them; a noun reads correctly with both.

decisions.choice: baharini (L); ziwani (B, R)
decisions.reason: The "sea" is the Sea of Galilee, beside Capernaum (meaning decision m4), a freshwater lake. Literal keeps the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say "ziwa", as the English says "lake".

decisions.choice: {{units:sarafu ya fedha yenye thamani ya mshahara wa siku nne|stateri}}
decisions.reason: As in the English and in John 6:7, the coin is given in wages by default, with the Greek coin as the alternative (meaning decision m2). "Ichukue" that follows agrees with either noun.

decisions.choice: {{units:một đồng bạc trị giá bốn ngày công|một đồng sta-te}} (B, R); "một đồng sta-te" (L)
decisions.reason: As in the English: the default says what the coin was worth, four drachmas, enough for two people's tax (meaning decision); the alternative and Literal keep the coin's name, transliterated.

decisions.choice: "biển" (L); "hồ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The sea is the Sea of Galilee by Capernaum (meaning decision); Balanced says "lake" here, as the English Balanced does, since a fishing line is cast from the shore.

decisions.choice: "걸려 넘어지게 하다" (L), "비위를 거스르다" (B), "마음을 상하게 하다" (R); "바다" (L, B), "호수" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of stumbling used for this verb in the Korean Matthew (15:12); the sense is giving them cause for offence (meaning decision). The sea is the Sea of Galilee, worded as settled for the Gospels.

decisions.choice: "{{units:나흘 품삯이 되는 은돈 한 닢|스타테르 한 닢}}" (B, R); "스타테르 한 닢" (L)
decisions.reason: A stater was a silver coin worth four drachmas (meaning decision), about four days' wages; the default says its worth, the alternative keeps the coin, as in the English. The particles that follow ("을" in B, "이" in R) fit both forms.

decisions.choice: {{units:የአራት ቀን ደመወዝ የሚያህል የብር ሳንቲም|አንድ እስታቴር}} (a silver coin worth four days' wages; a stater)
decisions.reason: A coin, so the default gives its value in days' wages, as the English does, and the alternative keeps its name; there is no metric form for money. Literal keeps "እስታቴር".

decisions.choice: {{units:серебряную монету, равную заработку за четыре дня|статир}}
decisions.reason: Coins have no metric form, so as in the English the default gives the coin's value in wages and the alternative names the coin. Literal keeps "статир".

decisions.choice: "море" (L); "озеро" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Sea of Galilee is a lake; Literal keeps the Greek word, as at 13:47.

decisions.choice: {{units:चार दिन की मज़दूरी के बराबर चाँदी का एक सिक्का|एक स्तातेर}}
decisions.reason: Coins have no metric form, so the default gives the value in wages and the units setting gives the coin, as the English does. Literal keeps "स्तातेर".

decisions.choice: "समुद्र" (L); "झील" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Sea of Galilee is a lake. Literal keeps the Greek "sea".

decisions.choice: "не стали для них причиною спотикання" (L); "не давати їм приводу обурюватися" (B); "не засмучувати" (R)
decisions.reason: Here skandalizō means giving the collectors cause to take offense, not making them fall from faith, so Balanced and Readable leave the book's usual "відпасти від віри"; "спокусити" now means to tempt.

decisions.choice: "море" (L); "озеро" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Gospels' convention for the Sea of Galilee: Literal keeps the Greek word, Balanced and Readable say what it is.

decisions.choice: "スタテル[銀貨]" (L); {{units:四日分の賃金にあたる銀貨一枚|スタテル銀貨一枚}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Coins have no metric form: the Measures setting gives the value in wages, with the coin as the alternative (m2), as the English does; Literal keeps the coin.
The sea is the Sea of Galilee by Capernaum (m4); Literal keeps the Greek word, and Balanced and Readable say it is a lake, as the English does.
